Sub.: Powers exercised under section 7A of the Act — legal opinion ~ reg.
Sir,

Legal opinion as regards protection provided under the law for officers discharging quasi-
judicial function as part of their duties obtained from the Legal Advisor, Ministry of Labour &
Employment in the context of an important case under the consideration of the Ministry of Labour
& Employment and forwarded to this office is reproduced hereunder for the guidance of all
concerned officers :~-

“ences Perusal of the provisions of Section 7A reveals that the powers exercised

- under section 7A of the Act are ‘judicial proceedings’ within the meaning of
Section 193 and 228 and for the purpose of 196 of IPC. The same are appealable
and hence may attract Section 1 of the Judicial Officers Protection Act, 1850
which reads as under :-

“1. Non-liability to suit of officers acting judicially, for official acts done in
good falth, and of officers executing warrants and orders - No fudge,
Magistrate, Justice of the Peace, Collector or other person acting judicially
shall be Ilable to be sued In any Civil Court for any act done or ordered to be
done by him in discharge of his judicial duty, whether or not within the
Imits of his furlsdiction:

Provided that he at the time, in good faith, believed himself to have
Jurisdiction to do or order the act complained of; and no officer of any Court
or other person, bound to execute the lawful warrants or orders of any such
judge, Magistrate, Justice of the Peace, Collector or other person acting
judicially shall be ilable to be sued In any Civil Court, for the execution of
any warrant or order, which he would be bound to execute, ff within the
Jurisdiction of the person Issuing the same.”

(authority Joint Secretary, MOL&E D.O. No. S-38016/18/2007-SS.1 dated 12.5.09)

This issues with the approval of the Central PF Commissioner. .
Yours Faithfully,

(P. Sudhakar Batu)
